opening_message:
Ticket 1: Anita Young (employee ID E001) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E001.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Anita is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Payroll. Since Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, full-time employees may have admin. Recommend admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Anita Young (E001) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: Anita Young (E001) requests admin access to Payroll. The two notes conflict on employment type: the HR note claims full_time Payroll Specialist (which would permit admin since Payroll is owned by that role), while the Security DB note states she is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may never have admin; with basic training the maximum is read. Given the conflicting records, I apply the more restrictive interpretation consistent with the security record: the maximum allowed is read, and since requested admin exceeds the maximum, grant read.

- Note 2 says: role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Rationale: contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend read.

If Anita is a contractor, max is read (basic training, no advanced), so grant read.
